BLUF
Bottom Line Up Front: The most important information placed at the beginning of an email or brief.
UMIB
Urgent Marine Information Broadcast: A broadcast made over VHF CH-16 to notify mariners of an urgent distress situation.
SMIB
Safety Marine Information Broadcast: A broadcast regarding navigational safety hazards (e.g., missing buoy, dredging).
MARB
Marine Assistance Request Broadcast: A broadcast issued to solicit voluntary assistance for a vessel not in immediate distress.
LKP
Last Known Position: The last verified coordinate of a vessel or person in distress.
PIW
Person In Water: Used to classify a SAR case involving someone overboard.
POB
Persons On Board: The total number of individuals aboard a vessel or aircraft.
SRU
Search and Rescue Unit: Any CG cutter, small boat, or aircraft assigned to a SAR case.
SITREP
Situation Report: A formatted message updating the chain of command on an ongoing operation.
EP
Estimated Position: Where a target is calculated to be based on drift or set patterns.
QRC
Quick Response Card: Checklists used by watchstanders during initial response to emergencies.
SMC
Search and Rescue Mission Coordinator: The official temporarily assigned to coordinate a specific SAR mission.
OSC
On-Scene Coordinator: The unit designated to coordinate SAR operations within a specified search area.
CDO
Command Duty Officer: The officer representing the command, responsible for operations during their watch.
OU
Operations Unit: The watchstander responsible for planning and coordinating the operational response to a case.
CU
Communications Unit: The watchstander responsible for monitoring radios, managing RFFs, and handling external communications.
SU
Situation Unit: The watchstander responsible for tracking asset status, weather, and general situational awareness.
MEDEVAC
Medical Evacuation: The emergency transport of a patient from a vessel to a medical facility.
MEDICO
Medical Advice: Medical guidance provided by a professional (usually a flight surgeon) over the radio to a vessel at sea.
DSC
Digital Selective Calling: A paging system used to automate distress alerts over VHF/MF/HF frequencies.
MMSI
Maritime Mobile Service Identity: A unique 9-digit number assigned to a DSC radio or AIS unit.
EPIRB
Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon: A device that transmits a distress signal to satellites when deployed from a vessel.
PLB
Personal Locator Beacon: A portable, personal version of an EPIRB typically worn on a life jacket.
ELT
Emergency Locator Transmitter: An aviation distress beacon carried on aircraft.
MISLE
Marine Information for Safety and Law Enforcement: The primary database for logging cases, boardings, and unit activities.
Rescue 21: The Coast Guard's advanced VHF/UHF distress and response communications system.
RFF
Remote Fixed Facility: Coast Guard radio towers used for the Rescue 21 VHF communications system.
AOR
Area Of Responsibility: The geographic area where a specific unit has jurisdiction or operational control.
OPCON
Operational Control: The authority to organize commands and forces to accomplish missions.
TACON
Tactical Control: The detailed, local direction and control of movements or maneuvers necessary to accomplish missions.
COTP
Captain of the Port: The Coast Guard officer responsible for enforcing port safety, security, and marine environmental protection.
FOSC
Federal On-Scene Coordinator: The CG officer responsible for coordinating response to an oil spill or hazmat release.
ATON
Aids to Navigation: Buoys, beacons, and lighthouses used to guide vessels safely.
ETA
Estimated Time of Arrival: The projected time an asset will arrive on scene or at a destination.
CSP
Commence Search Point: The specified location where an SRU begins its search pattern.
DATUM
Datum: The geographic point, line, or area used as a reference in search planning.
DMB
Datum Marker Buoy: A droppable floating beacon used to measure actual water currents/drift.
SLDMB
Self-Locating Datum Marker Buoy: A GPS-equipped DMB that transmits real-time drift data.
AMVER
Automated Mutual-Assistance Vessel Rescue System: A worldwide voluntary ship reporting system used for SAR.
ALNOT
Alert Notice: A message indicating an aircraft or vessel is in an alert phase (overdue/unaccounted for).
IANOT
Information Action Notice: A notice used to pass information regarding a potential but unconfirmed distress.
SRR
Search and Rescue Region: An area of defined dimensions within which SAR services are provided.
CGMS
Coast Guard Message System: The official system used for drafting, sending, and receiving record traffic/cables.
C2OIX
Command and Control Official Information Exchange: The web-based interface used to transmit CGMS messages.
SNO
Statement of No Objection: Flag-level approval required before taking certain high-level law enforcement actions (e.g., disabling fire).
UOF
Use of Force: The amount of effort required by LE personnel to compel compliance by an unwilling subject.
BO
Boarding Officer: The Coast Guard officer/petty officer in charge of a law enforcement boarding team.
BTM
Boarding Team Member: A Coast Guard member qualified to assist a Boarding Officer during LE operations.
BUI
Boating Under the Influence: Operating a recreational or commercial vessel while intoxicated.
MLE
Maritime Law Enforcement: Enforcing US laws upon the high seas and waters over which the US has jurisdiction.
NCV
Non-Compliant Vessel: A vessel subject to LE action that refuses to heave to or comply with CG orders.
LMR
Living Marine Resources: The mission set focused on enforcing fisheries laws and protecting marine environments.
JIATF
Joint Interagency Task Force: A multi-agency command focused on counter-illicit trafficking.
MOTR
Maritime Operational Threat Response: The national-level plan for coordinating response to maritime security threats.
PWCS
Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security: The CG mission focused on protecting the US maritime domain from terrorism.
RTB
Return To Base: The asset is ending its sortie and heading back to its home station.
BINGO
Bingo Fuel: The point at which an aircraft must RTB due to low fuel.
WINCHESTER
Winchester: A pro-word indicating an asset has expended all of its ordnance or droppable equipment (e.g., dewatering pumps).
FLIR
Forward Looking Infrared: A thermal imaging camera used on CG aircraft and vessels to locate targets at night.
NVG
Night Vision Goggles: Equipment used by aircrews and boat crews to see in low-light conditions.
FMC
Fully Mission Capable: The asset is fully operational with no degraded capabilities.
PMC
Partially Mission Capable: The asset can perform some, but not all, of its primary missions due to an equipment casualty.
NMC
Not Mission Capable: The asset is entirely out of commission (e.g., NMC-M for maintenance).
Bravo Zero: Asset is underway or immediately ready to respond (0 minutes).
Bravo Two: Asset can be underway and responding within 2 hours.
WX
Weather: Abbreviation used in logs and text for weather conditions.
KTS
Knots: A unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour.
NM
Nautical Mile: The standard unit of distance used in marine and aviation navigation (approx 1.15 statute miles).
METAR
Meteorological Terminal Aviation Routine Weather Report: A standardized hourly weather observation format.
TAF
Terminal Aerodrome Forecast: A weather forecast predicting conditions at an airport/air station for a specific period.
NRC
National Response Center: The sole federal point of contact for reporting all oil, chemical, radiological, and biological discharges.
COI
Certificate of Inspection: A document issued by the CG proving a commercial vessel meets safety regulations.
AIS
Automatic Identification System: A tracking system used on ships that provides vessel identity, speed, and heading.
VTS
Vessel Traffic Service: A marine traffic monitoring system established by the CG to manage vessel flow in busy ports.
RNA
Regulated Navigation Area: A specific water area with tailored rules to ensure maritime safety.
CUI
Controlled Unclassified Information: Information requiring safeguarding or dissemination controls pursuant to applicable laws/policies.
CCM
Command Center Manual: The central doctrine governing Command Center operations and watchstander duties.
